title: QBR - Nebula Retail Health Check
summary: Quarterly health-check focused on usage trends, cost drivers, reliability incidents, and roadmap alignment. Discussed moving to reserved capacity vs staying hosted, KV/prefix cache tuning, upcoming feature rollouts (streaming improvements, per-route dashboards), and security artifacts requested for procurement. Agreed next steps: share detailed usage+cost breakdown, schedule SE deep-dive for latency tail analysis, and send Dedicated pricing with commitment options.

Date: 2026-06-04
Time: 14:00 - 14:52 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording: yes
Agenda: QBR / health check - usage, costs, reliability, roadmap
transcript: 00:00:00 Avery (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is the QBR health check for Nebula Retail, I'm Avery (AE) from Redwood, joining with Marcus (SE) and Sofia (CSM). Quick roll call?
00:00:10 Lena (Nebula): Hi, Lena here. Sorry about the train noise, on my end. Carlos, Priya and Tom are here too.
00:00:22 Carlos (Nebula): Yep morning all, Carlos - engineering. We're excited to see the breakdowns.
00:00:31 Sofia (Redwood): Quick agenda — we'll walk usage trends, incidents, performance tuning suggestions, and then roadmap + security asks. Any additions?
00:00:40 Tom (Nebula): No additions, that covers it.

00:01:05 Marcus (Redwood): I'll start with the usage numbers. Over the last 90 days your token usage has grown ~28% month-over-month, average tokens/day now around 18M. There were two big spikes in late April and mid-May tied to marketing promos.
00:01:40 Carlos: Yeah the mid-May spike was from a promo we forgot to throttle. That cost hit was higher than expected — can you show cost per route?

00:02:00 Avery: Absolutely, we'll share the per-route cost CSV after the call. Top three cost drivers are: 1) product-recommendation route (long context), 2) chat-assist, 3) nightly batch re-ranks. The product-recommendation route has a lot of long contexts — 1,500 to 2,000 token lengths intermittently.
00:02:45 Lena: Right, long contexts are important for accuracy. We're worried about latency too — some customers report slower searches during peaks.
00:03:05 Marcus: We noticed p95 latency jumped from ~220ms to ~680ms during the largest spike. p50/p90 look fine but tail gets worse which points to KV cache misses and batching saturation.
00:03:32 Priya (Nebula): KV cache misses? We thought we had prefix caching enabled. Is that not working?

00:03:45 Marcus: Prefix cache is enabled but with the mix of dynamic prompts your hit-rate is around 42%, there's opportunity to increase caching by normalizing prompt templates and moving more context into shorter embeddings or stateful keys. Also consider increasing KV cache capacity on the route or using sticky routing for high-frequency users.
00:04:20 Tom: Sticky routing as in reserving the same worker for a user session? That could help but concerned about cost.

00:04:32 Avery: Correct, sticky sessions reduce cold starts and cache thrash. There's a tradeoff: slight increase in infra cost but lower tail latency and fewer expensive re-computations. We can model that in the cost deck.
00:05:00 Carlos: On the dedicated capacity topic — can you remind us of differences between hosted and dedicated again?

00:05:10 Avery: Hosted is great for bursty workloads, pay-as-you-go. Dedicated (Reserved) gives you guaranteed GPU pools, predictable throughput, and isolation — better p99 stability and often lower unit cost at scale with monthly commit. We can show a modeled ROI vs your current 90-day usage.
00:05:40 Lena: What's the committed utilization threshold where dedicated becomes cheaper?

00:05:50 Marcus: Roughly if sustained throughput is > 3–4 rps for your long-context routes continuously, Dedicated usually becomes cost-effective. But it depends on model family and quantization profile. We'll run a fit to your exact token mix.
00:06:20 Priya: We also need to confirm data residency and KMS keys — procurement asked about KMS/HSM integration and audit logs.

00:06:32 Sofia: We'll attach our SOC2 Type II report, network architecture for VPC peering, and KMS/HSM integration docs. We support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments and we have HSM integrations for enterprise. We'll drop those into the CRM folder after the call.
00:07:00 Tom: Great. Also re: incidents — we had that 3/23 disruption. Can you summarize root cause?

00:07:12 Marcus: The March 23rd incident was a multi-tenant GC pause on a serving node combined with a spike of large-context requests that exhausted connection pooling in one region; cache warming failed due to a rapid traffic shift. We've since rolled a kernel-level GC mitigation and adjusted autoscale thresholds. Error budget impact was ~0.4% for that day.
00:07:48 Carlos: That aligns with our logs. Are there recommended configuration changes to avoid recurrence?

00:07:57 Marcus: Yes — we suggest two short-term changes: increase connection pool size for the affected route and enable proactive cache warming for top 10 keys. Medium-term: consider Dedicated pools for that route to isolate noisy neighbors.
00:08:20 Lena: If we moved to Dedicated, what's the SLA bump?
00:08:27 Avery: Dedicated customers get SLA-backed uptime with tighter latency SLOs and a dedicated support SLA tier. We'll include exact numbers in the pricing proposal.
00:08:40 Priya: Any configuration that would lower our token cost besides dedicated? Quantization?

00:08:50 Marcus: Yes — we can quantize model variants for batch jobs like nightly re-ranks (int8/4) which reduces GPU memory and token cost, without much quality loss for that workload. Also intelligent batching and caching will reduce per-token compute. We'll propose a quantization profile per route.
00:09:15 Tom: Can you show a sample of the quantized model quality comparison?
00:09:22 Marcus: We'll include small eval snippets and quality delta metrics for the top-3 routes. Expect low regression for re-ranking, moderate for creative generation — we'll call that out.
00:09:45 Lena: On observability, we'd like per-route dashboards and token-level cost attribution sent to our finance team monthly. Can that be automated?
00:09:58 Sofia: Yes, we can create a per-route dashboard in the Console and set scheduled exports to your S3/billing account. We'll also add token-level cost breakdowns and a monthly CSV export.
00:10:20 Carlos: About rate limits, during spikes some requests hit 429s — is that on Redwood side?

00:10:28 Marcus: Those 429s were because of per-account concurrency limits combined with sudden surge; we can tune burst tokens or add burst capacity to avoid 429s. For long-term, Dedicated removes that shared throttling vector.
00:10:50 Tom: Any security or compliance gaps we should be worried about before procurement?

00:10:57 Sofia: From our side, we provide SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, SOC2, and optional VPC/on-prem arrangements. For sensitive PII flows, we recommend Private deployment or strong redaction and customer-managed keys. We'll include a recommended control set.
00:11:30 Lena: For Private, what's the lift for Nebula — we run on GCP and have strict network policies.

00:11:39 Marcus: Private VPC peering and a customer-managed control plane is straightforward; on-prem is heavier. We'll provide a checklist: network ports, firewall rules, KMS endpoints, and expected infra specs.
00:12:05 Carlos: Back to costs — can you give a sample math for our May spike so procurement can see the delta?

00:12:13 Avery: We'll include a sample calc in the follow-up — e.g., the promo week added ~120M extra tokens, which at current hosted rates was ~$14k extra. With Dedicated you could have shaved 20–35% off per-token cost in that cohort depending on commit level.
00:12:40 Tom: That would help our finance case. Also, curious about the streaming improvements you mentioned in the roadmap — any ETA?

00:12:49 Marcus: We have a streaming runtime update in Q3 that reduces first-byte latency for medium-length responses and improves stability for function/tool-calling patterns. We'll share the public roadmap link.
00:13:10 Priya: Can we get a sample of the per-route dashboard and how alerts are configured?
00:13:18 Sofia: Yes, we'll provision a sample dashboard and a runbook for alerts; can also set alert thresholds for p95/p99 and error rate.
00:13:40 Carlos: One operational ask — for our data pipeline, we'd like token-level logs exported to BigQuery for our own analytics. Is that possible?
00:13:49 Avery: We support exports to S3/BigQuery via scheduled jobs; we'll include a config snippet and retention options.

00:14:12 Marcus: Quick note on a micro-optimization: your recommender often includes full product meta in the prompt. If you instead pass a short product id and use an embedding lookup to provide context, you can reduce prompt tokens by ~40% on that route.
00:14:40 Lena: Hmm, that might impact freshness. We'll have the data team evaluate.
00:15:05 Tom: Any A/B testing support for rollouts? We're planning a canary for the recommender change.
00:15:13 Marcus: Yes we support canary rollouts and A/B via rollout policies in the Console. You can route X% traffic to a variant and automatically rollback on quality regression.
00:15:30 Carlos: We'll want automatic rollback on any >1% degradation in conversion uplift — can that be instrumented?
00:15:38 Sofia: We can wire up quality monitors and tie to auto-rollbacks; requires a baseline eval set and the conversion signal hooked into our tracing. We'll help with the eval harness.
00:16:10 Lena: On billing, we need a line item break for embeddings vs generation. Our legal team asks for clear invoice lines.
00:16:20 Avery: We can export per-feature lines and tag by route. I'll add that to the follow-up export.
00:16:45 Tom: How about support SLAs if we move to Dedicated?
00:16:52 Avery: Dedicated includes priority support with 1-hour P1 response and a named TAM at higher tiers. We'll call out the tiers in the proposal.
00:17:20 Priya: For the latency deep-dive, what telemetry do you need from our side?

00:17:27 Marcus: Traces, p95/p99 histograms, sample request/response pairs, and mapping of user-id to session traces if possible. If you can provide a week of logs centered on a spike event that helps.
00:17:50 Carlos: We can provide that. We'll strip PII and share an anonymized set.
00:18:10 Marcus: Great. We'll run a replay and look at KV hit patterns and batching saturation. Expect a 30–45 minute session where we push a few synthetic loads to reproduce the tail.
00:18:40 Lena: Any risks in running synthetic loads against production?
00:18:47 Marcus: We'll run them in a controlled, low-volume window and coordinate with your infra. Alternatively, we can run it against a staging mirror if you have one.
00:19:10 Tom: Staging is flaky; better to do a controlled production test early morning.
00:19:20 Sofia: We'll schedule the deep-dive for a UTC off-peak window per your preference.
00:19:50 Avery: Ok switching to roadmap: Q3 runtime improvements, dedicated pooling enhancements, and per-route cost controls. We'll share release dates. Anything from Nebula you want prioritized?
00:20:00 Lena: Lower tail latency for recommender and a per-route cost alarm would be high impact for us.
00:20:10 Avery: Noted — we'll flag as a priority and discuss feasibility on the product side.
00:20:30 Carlos: Quick question — do you support model pinning per route? We want to avoid accidental model upgrades during experiments.
00:20:38 Marcus: Yes, model pinning and versioned rollouts are supported; you can pin route to a specific model SHA and only update via rollout.
00:21:00 Tom: On data retention, we need confirmation you don't store ephemeral prompts for Hosted customers beyond 30 days — procurement asked for explicit policy.

00:21:10 Sofia: Our default retention is 30 days for transient request logs; request/response retention and retention policies are configurable, and for Private you control retention entirely. We'll include the data-retention policy doc.
00:21:40 Carlos: Any network considerations for peering? We run GCP us-east4.
00:21:48 Marcus: We support peering in us-east4; we'll provide CIDR ranges and recommended egress rules. For Private we'll give a checklist.
00:22:10 Lena: Can we talk about cost modeling for a mid-sized Dedicated commit — say 3 GPUs for 12 months?

00:22:22 Avery: We'll run a modeled ROI comparing current hosted spend and 3-GPU monthly commit. I'll include assumptions: 80% sustained utilization, model family used (gptx-4-ish), and expected quantization gains.
00:22:50 Priya: One more ops ask — can we tag routes with our internal cost center tags so billing flows into our showback?
00:22:58 Sofia: Yes, route-level tags map to billing tags; we'll set that up in the Console and automate exports.

00:23:20 Marcus: Circling back to the KV hit rate — simple prompt normalization and moving heavy context to an embeddings store would boost hit-rate from 42% to likely >70%, cutting compute cost materially. We'll sketch a migration plan.
00:23:45 Carlos: Migration lift estimate?

00:23:50 Marcus: For the recommender, initial engineering effort ~2-3 sprint weeks to build an embeddings cache + lookup pattern and update prompts; plus a small infra config change. We can help with a proof-of-concept.
00:24:20 Lena: We'd like Redwood to run the POC with our engineers — what's the onboarding time?
00:24:28 Sofia: We typically run a 4-week POC: week 1 discovery, week 2 integration, week 3 testing, week 4 optimization and handoff. We'll scope in the proposal.
00:24:55 Tom: Cost for that POC?
00:25:00 Avery: We can offer a discounted POC rate and apply credit toward committed capacity if you convert. Exact numbers in the pricing doc.
00:25:25 Carlos: Ok that's helpful. Anything else on the tech side?
00:25:30 Marcus: One final perf note — enabling continuous batching on your high-throughput endpoints yields better throughput with small latency impact; we recommend a 10% batch-size cap to start.
00:25:50 Priya: We'll try that on dev first.
00:26:10 Lena: On procurement timeline, we aim to close a Dedicated decision by end of June, contingent on finance sign-off.
00:26:20 Avery: Good to know — we'll prioritize the pricing proposal early next week.
00:26:40 Sofia: Quick recap of what we'll send: usage + cost CSV, Dedicated pricing, SOC2 & KMS docs, and schedule for the latency deep-dive. Anything missing?
00:26:52 Carlos: Also include the per-route dashboard sample and the quantization quality snippets.
00:27:10 Avery: Noted. Any final questions from the Nebula team?
00:27:18 Tom: None from me.
00:27:30 Lena: One more — can you include a sample contract term where we reserve burst capacity? Procurement asked if bursts are included in commits.
00:27:40 Avery: We'll include burst clauses and a sample SLA appendix in the proposal.
00:28:00 Marcus: We'll also add a short runbook for cache-warming and connection pool tuning as immediate mitigations for tail latency.
00:28:20 Priya: Sounds good. We'll coordinate the deep-dive times after the call.
00:28:35 Sofia: Great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with all artifacts via the CRM link and send calendar invites for the deep-dive.
00:28:45 Lena: Thanks all, appreciate it.
00:29:00 [meeting continues with side discussions and scheduling logistics — 20 more minutes covering dates and follow-up details, some cross-talk]

00:45:12 Avery: Wrapping up — again, expect the deck and CSV by Tuesday, SOC2 & KMS docs by end of Friday, and Marcus will reach out to schedule the technical deep-dive for next week morning UTC off-peak.
00:45:30 Carlos: Thanks Avery, Marcus, Sofia. Looking forward to the proposal.
00:45:40 Marcus: Thanks everyone, bye.
00:46:00 [recording ends]
